reports.title: GeneDx Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

lines: •Reiterating full year 2026 revenue guidance of $475 to $490 million

desk.headline: Revenue up 5% to $123.1m, beat; 2026 sales range kept but exome/genome growth targets cut

other.label: Adjusted gross margin
other.change: vs 73.8% a year ago, 70.4% in Q2

results: Revenue rose 5% to $123.1m; core exome and genome revenue grew 12% to $110.4m while older panel tests fell to $9.7m from $14.6m.
Exome and genome test volume rose 25% to 32,134, with orders (accessions) up 28%.
Adjusted gross margin improved to 72% from 70% in Q2 but was below 74% a year ago; adjusted EPS was $0.28 vs a $0.07 estimate.
On a GAAP basis GeneDx lost $12.3m ($0.41 a share) as selling and admin costs rose to $79.1m.
Nine-month operating cash flow was -$72.0m; long-term debt is $146.2m and cash and securities $171.1m.

guidance.summary: GeneDx kept 2026 revenue at $475-490m, but cut its exome/genome volume and revenue growth targets while lifting its margin and profit outlook. It guided Q4 revenue to about $135m.

points: Management blamed the volume shortfall on insurers asking for paperwork up front, which led to cancelled, downgraded or delayed orders.
Average reimbursement per test rose 5% q/q to about $3,436, with about $3,500 expected in Q4; genome collection rates improved.
The new sales team calling on general paediatricians was said to already cover its cost and is seen as the main 2027 volume driver.
Management flagged Medicare lab-fee (PAMA) changes as a mid-single-digit hit to 2027 revenue, which it expects billing improvements to offset.
call.source: Call coverage: GeneDx Crushes EPS Consensus On Margin Gains, But Lower Volume Guidance Exposes A Business Trading Growth For Profitability — Earnings Whispers (via Finviz), 9 Nov 2026

watch: Q4 test volume against the 34,500 target and whether payer paperwork friction eases.
Reimbursement per test and the size of the 2027 PAMA hit.
Cash burn and debt after a $72m nine-month operating outflow.
